'''Kang Lung Wang''' ({{Lang-zh|t=王康隆}}; born 1941) is a Taiwanese physicist and [[electrical engineer]] specializing in [[nanotechnology]], [[Semiconductor|semiconductors]], and [[quantum systems]]. He is the Raytheon Chair in Electrical Engineering at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), where he leads its Device Research Laboratory. He was previously a professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT).  

== Early life and education ==
Wang was born in [[Lukang, Changhua]], Taiwan, in 1941. After high school, he graduated from [[National Cheng Kung University]] with a [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in 1964. He then earned an [[M.S.]] and his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] (MIT) in 1966 and 1970, respectively.<ref name="Liberty Times">{{Cite web|url=http://news.ltn.com.tw/news/weeklybiz/paper/1230846|title=〈人物專訪〉高職生變成中研院、工研院雙院士 王康隆找到自己喜歡的工作|date=2018-09-10|agency=[[Liberty Times]]|language=zh-TW}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation was titled, "Electron impact ionization cross sections for carbon vapor".<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wang |first=Kang L. |date=August 1970 |title=Electron impact ionization cross sections for carbon vapor |url=https://dspace.mit.edu/bitstream/handle/1721.1/13799/24510982-MIT.pdf?sequence=2 |access-date=12 January 2025 |publisher=[[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] |type=PhD Thesis}}</ref>

== Academic career ==
After receiving his doctorate, Wang was an assistant professor at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] from 1970 to 1972. He then worked as a physicist and engineer at the [[General Electric Research Laboratory]] from 1972 to 1979. Since 1979, he has been a professor at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]] (UCLA), and from 1993 to 1996 he served as the chair of the electrical engineering department at UCLA. From 2000 to 2002, he was dean of the School of Engineering at the [[Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]]. Between 2003 and 2013, he served as Director of the MARCO Focus Center on Functional Engineered Nano-Architectonics, and from 2007 to 2013 he was also Associate Director of the [[California NanoSystems Institute]]. From 2006 to the present, he has held the position of Raytheon Chair Professor of Physical Electronics and served as Director of the [[Western Institute of Nanoelectronics]]. He was the editor-in-chief of [[IEEE Transactions on Nanotechnology|''IEEE Transactions on Nanotechnology'']] from 2011 to 2014.

Wang serves on the editorial board of the ''Encyclopedia of Nanoscience and Nanotechnology'' (American Scientific publishers). He currently also serves as the Director of Marco Focus Center on [[Functional Engineered Nano Architectonics]], an interdisciplinary research center funded by [[Semiconductor Industry Association]] and the [[United States Department of Defense|Department of Defense]] to address the need of information processing technology beyond scaled [[CMOS]].  

He is also the director of the [[Western Institute of Nanoelectronics]] (WIN), a coordinated multi-project research institute. WIN is funded by the NRI, Intel, and the [[State of California]]. The current on-going projects are aimed at spintronics for low power applications. He currently serves as the editor-in-chief for the journal ''[[IEEE Transactions on Nanotechnology]]''.<ref>{{cite web|title=IEEE Transactions on Nanotechnology, Kang Wang EiC|url=https://site.ieee.org/tnano/kang-wang-eic/}}</ref> He was also the founding director of Nanoelectronics Research Facility at UCLA (established in 1989). In addition to these technical leadership contributions, he has provided academic leadership in [[engineering education]]. He was also the Dean of Engineering from 2000 to 2002 at the [[Hong Kong University of Science and Technology]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.seng.ust.hk/CDROM02/foreword/index.html |title=Forward, School of Engineering}}</ref>

== Research ==
Wang's research activities focus on [[nanotechnology]] and [[semiconductor]] nano devices. Specific topics include:
* [[Nanoscopic scale|nanoscale]] science: [[nanoelectronics]], [[nanoarchitecture]]s, and [[nanomagnet]]ics
* [[Spintronics|spintronic]] materials and devices
* quantum systems: self-assembly growth of quantum structures and cooperative assembly of [[quantum dot]] arrays; [[electron spin]] and coherence properties of [[SiGe]] and [[InAs]] quantum structures for implementation of spin-based quantum information
* silicon-based [[Molecular beam epitax|molecular beam epitaxy]]; nano-epitaxy of hetero-structures
* nonvolatile electronics and low-dissipation devices
* [[optoelectronics]], solar cells, and [[microwave]] devices

He was the inventor of strained layer [[MOSFET]], quantum SRAM cell, and band-aligned [[superlattice]]s. He holds 45 [[patent]]s and has published over 700 papers.

In 2018, the International Union of Pure and Applied Physics (IUPAP) recognized Wang for his discovery of chiral [[Majorana fermion|Majorana fermions]] and his contributions to spintronics.<ref>{{Cite web |date=Apr 18, 2018 |title=Kang Wang awarded international honor for seminal discovery in magnetism |url=https://samueli.ucla.edu/deep-learning-transforms-smartphone-microscopes-into-laboratory-grade-devices-2/ |access-date=2025-05-18 |website=UCLA Samueli |place=University of California Los Angeles |language=}}</ref>

2018: Magnetism award and Nēel Medal, International Union of Pure and Applied Physics [http://iupap.org/commissions/c9-magnetism/c9-awards/]

2018: Laureate of Industrial Technology Research Institute, Taiwan [https://www.itri.org.tw/chi/Content/MessagessPIC/List01.aspx?SiteID=1&MmmID=620602517410464211]

2018: Dr. Dan S. Louie lifetime achievement award [http://camla.org/annual-historymakers-awards-gala/] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181216122125/http://camla.org/annual-historymakers-awards-gala/ |date=2018-12-16 }} 

2017: [[J. J. Ebers Award]] by IEEE International Electron Devices Society [https://www.ee.ucla.edu/distinguished-prof-kang-l-wang-was-presented-the-2017-j-j-ebers-award-by-the-ieee-electron-devices-society-during-the-international-electron-devices-meeting/]

2017: Fellow, APS (American Physical Society)<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=www.aps.org|accessdate=16 September 2018}}</ref>

2016: Academician of Academia Sinica, Taiwan<ref>{{cite news |title=Kang-Lung Wang |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=701&_lang=en |access-date=18 March 2022 |agency=Academia Sinica}}</ref>

2015: Pan Wen Yuan Outstanding Research Award, Hsinchu, Taiwan

2012: Outstanding Alumni Award of National Cheng Kung University, Taiwan

2009: Semiconductor Industry Award Research Award

2007: IBM Faculty Award

1996: Semiconductor Research Corporation Technical Excellency Award

1992: Fellow, IEEE (Institute of Electrical and Electronics)

1987–88: Guggenheim Fellow Award, [[Max Planck Institute]], [[Germany]]

== Personal life ==
Wang met his wife, Edith Wang, while they were both graduate students at MIT. They have two sons and a daughter, [[Evelyn Wang]].
